title: dir2mcp_ask
description: Tool contract document containing nested input and output schemas for RAG answers with citations; can run search-only mode.

k.description: Number of hits to return. Bound 1..50. An OMITTED field resolves to the server's configured rag.k_default (SPEC 16), so a served schema reports that effective value as this field's default (SPEC 9.1). The canonical schema carries no literal default, because the value is per deployment.

languages.description: Optional (SPEC §9.5): restrict retrieved contexts to representations recorded in any of these BCP-47 languages (case-insensitive primary-subtag match). Absent/empty = no filtering; unknown-language representations never match a specific filter.

date_from.description: Optional (SPEC §9.6): RFC 3339 timestamp or bare YYYY-MM-DD date; exclude contexts from documents dated before this (inclusive; a bare date = start of that day UTC). Absent = open lower bound.

date_to.description: Optional (SPEC §9.6): RFC 3339 timestamp or bare YYYY-MM-DD date; exclude contexts from documents dated after this (inclusive; a bare date = end of that day UTC). Absent = open upper bound.

time_from_ms.description: Optional (SPEC §9.8): intra-document media time-window lower bound, in milliseconds within a document's timeline (§5.4). When set, only time-spanned contexts are eligible and are kept iff their span overlaps [time_from_ms, time_to_ms] (inclusive). Absent = open lower bound. time_from_ms > time_to_ms is INVALID_FIELD.

time_to_ms.description: Optional (SPEC §9.8): intra-document media time-window upper bound, in milliseconds within a document's timeline (§5.4). Absent = open upper bound.

evidence.description: Absolute evidence verdict of the ELIGIBLE hit set behind the answer. Aggregation is normative (SPEC 9.4.3): the strongest eligible hit's verdict, ordered strong > sufficient > insufficient, with unknown only when no eligible hit carries an absolute signal. insufficient is the structured form of the abstention 9.4.3 requires a caller to be able to distinguish. Never a raw score (SPEC 9.1.1). Optional; a server MUST NOT emit it unless it advertises a schema that declares it.

faithfulness.description: Whether the published answer was checked against the retrieved passages the model was shown, and what that check concluded (SPEC 9.4.4). verified: every claim was supported. unsupported: at least one claim was not, and the server therefore WITHHELD the answer, so `answer` carries a refusal and `citations` is empty. unchecked: verification produced no verdict (not configured, or attempted and unable to complete), which is the default and is NOT a quality signal. Orthogonal to `evidence`: that verdict describes the RETRIEVAL, this one describes the ANSWER, and a withheld answer may sit on strong evidence. Optional; a server MUST NOT emit it unless it advertises a schema that declares it.
